items: ★ Imminent danger → **constant observation, remove hazards, emergency psychiatric evaluation/hospitalization**
Voluntary admission preferred; involuntary protection if serious danger and refusal, following local law
Treat poisoning/injury first; address agitation, withdrawal, mood/psychotic disorder and underlying medical illness
Low acute risk with reliable support → outpatient care only with collaborative plan and rapid follow-up

rows.label: Complications
items: Fatal or repeated attempts, hypoxic injury, disability, caregiver distress
High vulnerability after emergency/inpatient discharge; abrupt loss of contact raises concern

rows.label: Prevention
items: ★ **Safety plan**: warning signs, coping actions, supportive contacts, professional crisis resources, emergency escalation
★ **Lethal means restriction**: secure/remove firearms, limit medication quantities; enlist trusted support
Arrange prompt follow-up and active care linkage; identify reasons for living and dependable supervision

rows.label: Mimics
items: Nonsuicidal self-injury: no intent to die, but future suicide risk still elevated
Passive death wish: no active plan, still warrants full evaluation
Obsessive intrusive harm thoughts: unwanted/ego-dystonic, without desire or intent to act

suicide-risk-assessment.evidence: Not checked online; established clinical suicide-risk assessment and safety-planning principles; detention law varies locally.

toxic-alcohol-poisoning.name: Toxic alcohol poisoning
toxic-alcohol-poisoning.scope: Ethylene glycol (calcium oxalate, renal failure), methanol (visual impairment, optic disc hyperemia), isopropyl alcohol (ketosis without acidosis), osmolar gap, fomepizole, hemodialysis
toxic-alcohol-poisoning.core: Unexplained intoxication with an osmolar gap suggests toxic alcohol exposure; delayed organic-acid accumulation can produce profound anion-gap acidosis.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Antifreeze, windshield-washer fluid, solvents; accidental ingestion or self-harm; substitute alcohol consumption

rows.label: Clues
items: Vomiting, abdominal pain, altered consciousness; tachypnea or shock signals severe toxicity
★ **Normal osmolar gap does not exclude late poisoning**; history may be unavailable

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Alcohol dehydrogenase converts parent alcohols into characteristic metabolites
Parent compounds elevate osmolar gap early; metabolites later raise anion gap in acid-producing ingestions

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ Electrolytes, ABG/VBG, glucose, BUN, measured osmolality, ethanol and specific alcohol levels
Calculated osmolality = 2Na + glucose/18 + BUN/2.8; add ethanol/4.6, concentrations in mg/dL
Measured minus calculated >10 mOsm/kg supports exposure; nonspecific and time-dependent
Urinalysis and calcium/creatinine assess organ injury; absent characteristic sediment inclusions do not exclude exposure

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ Airway, IV fluids, poison-center consultation; **fomepizole** immediately for suspected methanol/ethylene glycol
Methanol: vision loss, coma/seizures or pH ≤7.15 → **hemodialysis**; ethylene glycol: severe acidosis/AKI → dialysis
Sodium bicarbonate for marked acidemia; methanol → folinic acid; ethylene glycol → thiamine/pyridoxine adjuncts
★ Isopropanol → supportive care; **avoid fomepizole**, which prolongs parent-compound toxicity

rows.label: Complications
items: Methanol: permanent blindness, basal ganglia injury
Oxalate toxicity: hypocalcemic dysrhythmias; any ingestion: aspiration, coma, death

rows.label: Prevention
items: Store products separately from beverages; child-resistant containers; suicide-risk assessment after intentional ingestion

rows.label: Mimics
items: DKA: hyperglycemia and β-hydroxybutyrate elevation
Alcoholic ketoacidosis: poor intake after alcohol binge, low/normal glucose

toxic-alcohol-poisoning.evidence: Checked 2026-10-30: [EXTRIP methanol](https://www.extrip-workgroup.org/methanol), [ethylene glycol](https://www.extrip-workgroup.org/ethylene-glycol); other principles: established toxicology teaching.

wernicke-korsakoff-syndrome.name: Wernicke-Korsakoff syndrome
wernicke-korsakoff-syndrome.scope: Wernicke encephalopathy (triad of encephalopathy, ataxia, oculomotor dysfunction), Korsakoff psychosis (confabulation, amnesia), thiamine (B1) deficiency, IV thiamine before glucose, mammillary body atrophy
wernicke-korsakoff-syndrome.core: Malnourished adult with confusion, gait ataxia, or ophthalmoplegia/nystagmus; the complete Wernicke triad is often absent.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Alcohol use disorder, hyperemesis gravidarum, bariatric surgery, starvation, inadequate parenteral nutrition
Carbohydrate loading or refeeding increases thiamine demand in depleted patients

rows.label: Clues
items: Hypothermia, hypotension, or coma signal severe deficiency
★ Korsakoff: disproportionate **anterograde amnesia**, retrograde memory loss, confabulation; relatively preserved alertness

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Thiamine deficiency impairs carbohydrate metabolism → ATP failure and selective neuronal injury
Medial thalami, periaqueductal gray, mammillary bodies injured → persistent amnestic syndrome

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ **Clinical diagnosis**; do not wait for vitamin assays or imaging before treatment
MRI may show symmetric thalamic/periaqueductal lesions; normal MRI does not exclude Wernicke
Chronic disease: mammillary body atrophy; evaluate glucose, electrolytes, magnesium, and competing encephalopathy causes

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ Suspected Wernicke → **high-dose IV thiamine**, followed by oral replacement after stabilization
Give thiamine before or with glucose when feasible; never delay emergency dextrose for hypoglycemia
Replete magnesium, fluid/electrolyte deficits; restore nutrition cautiously and treat alcohol withdrawal separately
Ocular findings may improve rapidly; gait/cognition recover more slowly; established amnesia often persists

rows.label: Complications
items: Untreated encephalopathy → death or irreversible Korsakoff syndrome; falls and impaired independent living
Refeeding syndrome → hypophosphatemia, arrhythmias, respiratory weakness

rows.label: Prevention
items: ★ Routine oral **thiamine supplementation** for persistent malnutrition; nutritional assessment during alcohol treatment
Alcohol cessation support, balanced nutrition; monitor intake after bariatric surgery or prolonged vomiting

rows.label: Mimics
items: Alcohol withdrawal delirium: autonomic hyperactivity, tremor, hallucinations after reduced intake
Hepatic encephalopathy: cirrhosis, asterixis, precipitating bleed or infection
Posterior circulation stroke: abrupt focal deficits; diffusion MRI identifies infarction

wernicke-korsakoff-syndrome.evidence: Not checked online; established thiamine-deficiency teaching.
